newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bomb wounds 20 in an Algiers cinema - official.
newsitem.headline: Bomb wounds 20 in an Algiers cinema - official.

text.p: A home-made bomb exploded inside a cinema in a working-class district of Algiers on Wednesday, wounding 20 moviegoers, one of them seriously, the official Algerian news agency APS reported.
"The bomb went off at around 1445 (local time) inside Le Musset Cinema in Belouizdad district...20 people were wounded including one in a serious state," APS quoted security forces as saying.
Earlier, residents speaking to Reuters by telephone from the Algerian capital described the scene at the blast, the latest in a series of bombings in the Algerian capital.
"The blast occured at the upper circle of the cinema. The bomb was hidden in a plastic bag," said one resident.
At the end of May, at least five people were wounded when a bomb ripped through a cinema in Algiers.
Two bombs killed seven people on buses in Algiers on June 1. More than 40 passengers were wounded in a bomb on a train in late June.
The rash of bombings prompted Algiers authorities in late June to announce fresh security measures for the capital to try to thwart attacks by Moslem guerrillas.
The measures made it compulsory for officials at cinema, trains, buses and other public places to carry out security checks on people and cars.
About 60,000 people have been killed in political violence since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.
